title: "Visualizing Chipotle's Data - Solutions"
output: html_document

This time we are going to pull data directly from the internet.
Special thanks to: https://github.com/justmarkham for sharing the dataset and materials.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/chipotle.tsv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called chipo.

```{r}
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justmarkham/DAT8/master/data/chipotle.tsv"

chipo <- read_tsv(url, na = c("", "NA", "NULL"))
```

### Step 4. See the first 10 entries

```{r}
head(chipo, 10)
```

### Step 5. Create a histogram of the top 5 items bought

```{r}
# count how many times each item appears and keep the top 5
top5 <- chipo |>
  count(item_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(5)

# create the plot
ggplot(top5, aes(x = reorder(item_name, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  # set the title and labels
  labs(x = "Items", y = "Number of Times Ordered",
       title = "Most ordered Chipotle's Items")
```

### Step 6. Create a scatterplot with the number of items orderered per order price

#### Hint: Price should be in the X-axis and Items ordered in the Y-axis

```{r}
# strip the dollar sign and convert the price to a number
chipo <- chipo |> mutate(item_price = as.numeric(str_remove(item_price, fixed("$"))))

# then group by the orders and sum
orders <- chipo |>
  group_by(order_id) |>
  summarise(item_price = sum(item_price), quantity = sum(quantity))

# create the scatterplot
ggplot(orders, aes(x = item_price, y = quantity)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "green") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Order Price", y = "Items ordered",
       title = "Number of items ordered per order price")
```
